name: Legacy Senior Residences
award: 2022 Federal 4% and state housing tax credits (Round Two)
headline: Legacy Senior Residences is a 72-apartment, three-story building for adults 55 and older at Sheridan Boulevard and W. 64th Avenue in Arvada, developed by Cornerstone Housing Group with the Arvada Housing Authority, with 8 voucher units for seniors leaving homelessness; after missing in 2021 it won $1,078,412 a year in federal 4% credit and $1,000,000 in state credit in CHFA's 2022 Round Two.
why_it_matters: It delivers a City Council senior-housing goal on a tight infill site with city-mandated road and drainage work, using Arvada's own bond cap, an $840,000 city loan, 8 project-based vouchers tied to the city's Homeless Navigation Program and a housing authority partnership for tax exemption.

status.label: Credits awarded; construction and opening not confirmed by a retrievable dated record
status.detail: Arvada's address file shows the city retired the 5430 W 64th Ave address as replatted and assigned 5353 W 63rd Ave to a 72-unit Legacy Senior Residences building on 2023-05-22. That shows platting and addressing, not construction; no permit, closing, groundbreaking or opening record could be retrieved from a public page.

background.text: Arvada City Council set a goal of a senior attainable housing development of 50 or more units by 2019; Legacy is the project meant to meet it.

The project first applied in CHFA's 2021 Round Two (requesting $929,622 of federal credit, $1,000,000 of state credit and $13,810,000 of bonds) and was not on that round's award report; for 2022 it dropped income averaging for fixed 30%, 50% and 60% AMI set-asides.
In February 2022 the project asked for $12,600,000 of bond cap from CHFA's 4% PAB pool.
Cornerstone bought the land in 2021 for $1,800,000 ($25,000 per unit).
Approvals: multifamily use by right; Preliminary Development Plan approved in 2019; Final Development Plan expected August 2022.

The city required Benton Street to be extended through the site, 0.5 acre ($163,500) dedicated for a new W 63rd Ave, a private access road with a city easement, a larger detention pond taking neighboring runoff and buried utility lines; expansive soils forced helical piers and a full crawl space.
Arvada's address file retired 5430 W 64th Ave as replatted and assigned 5353 W 63rd Ave to the 72-unit building in May 2023, consistent with the new W 63rd Ave.
No asterisk footnote applies to this row in the award report; its asterisks only key the Type and Target codes.
